s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain with progressive renal failure and obstructive uropathy
salient_findings: Lower abdominal pain and decreased bowel movements
Left lower-quadrant pain and low-grade fevers
Confluent retroperitoneal soft-tissue mass encasing surrounding vessels
Progressively worsening epigastric pain with nausea and vomiting
Bilateral hydronephrosis with extrinsic compression and medial deviation of the ureters
key_facts: 50-year-old woman with hypertension and COPD
Initial presentation with lower abdominal pain and decreased bowel movements
Diagnosed with constipation
Treated with ciprofloxacin and metronidazole for presumed diverticulitis
Abdominal CT revealed a confluent retroperitoneal soft-tissue mass
HIDA scan confirmed cholecystitis
Underwent cholecystectomy
Post-surgery symptoms included epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, and fatigue
Denies fevers, chills, dysuria, or GI bleeding
Slight epigastric tenderness without guarding on exam
Elevated creatinine level (8.18 mg/dL) with baseline of 0.8
Mild bilateral hydronephrosis on renal ultrasound
Extrinsic compression and medial deviation of the ureters on retrograde pyelogram

shortlist.label: Retroperitoneal fibrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Confluent retroperitoneal soft-tissue mass and extrinsic compression of ureters

shortlist.label: Retroperitoneal sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Retroperitoneal soft-tissue mass and progressive renal failure

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a confluent retroperitoneal soft-tissue mass encasing surrounding vessels, bilateral hydronephrosis, and extrinsic compression of the ureters is most consistent with retroperitoneal fibrosis, which can cause ureteral obstruction and renal impairment.

rejected.label: Retroperitoneal sarcoma
rejected.why: While a retroperitoneal sarcoma could cause a mass and obstruction, the patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more suggestive of a fibrotic process rather than a malignant tumor.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphoma could cause retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy and obstruction, but the patient's imaging findings and clinical presentation are not typical for lymphoma.

rejected.label: Metastatic cancer
rejected.why: Metastatic cancer could cause retroperitoneal lymph node metastasis and obstruction, but the patient's history and imaging findings do not suggest a primary malignancy.

rejected.label: Retroperitoneal lymph node metastasis
rejected.why: This diagnosis is similar to metastatic cancer and is not supported by the patient's history and imaging findings.
